analysis: Leishmaniasis is a disease caused by protozoan parasites, primarily transmitted by sandflies. In Spain, it is not eradicated (option opa is incorrect), and it is primarily zoonotic rather than anthroponotic (option opb is incorrect). However, leishmaniasis can indeed be associated with HIV, as co-infection can lead to more severe manifestations of the disease (option opc is correct). The disease is transmitted by Phlebotomus sandflies, not Lutzomyia (option opd is incorrect), and it has both visceral and cutaneous forms, meaning it is not exclusively visceral (option ope is incorrect). Therefore, the best-supported option is that leishmaniasis is associated with HIV.
